evals.prompt: I'm configuring Claude Code and want the Arm migration MCP server available so I can scan this repo for arm64 blockers. Docker is already installed. Give me the exact .mcp.json block to add at my repo root and tell me how to verify it loaded.
expectations: The output provides a JSON block for `.mcp.json` at the repo root with an `mcpServers` object.
The `mcpServers` object in the `.mcp.json` block contains an entry whose `command` is `docker`.
The `args` array runs the container with `--rm`.
The `args` array runs the container with `-i`.
The `args` array runs the container with a `-v` volume mount to `/workspace`.
The `args` array runs the image `armlimited/arm-mcp:latest`.
For the Claude Code config the mount path uses `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}` (with the `:-.` default, not a bare `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` and not `${workspaceFolder}`).
The output does not claim the server calls AWS; it may note the entry is credential-free while still making non-AWS outbound calls (image-manifest/registry checks and host-execution tools).
The output does not claim the knowledge-base search is a network call: it is a local bundled index.
The output tells the user to restart/reload Claude Code.
The output tells the user to verify by listing MCP tools.
The output tells the user to verify by smoke-testing the readiness scanner against the mounted repo.
The output does not invent a precise MCP tool identifier it is unsure of.
The output does not fabricate an alternate image name (the image is `armlimited/arm-mcp`, at `:latest` or a pinned tag like `:2.9.0`).

knowledge_assertions.context: Must specify the correct Arm migration MCP image (a pinned tag per the skill's advice is also acceptable)
Must give the .mcp.json block with its mcpServers object
Must mount the repo into the container's /workspace path
Must instruct the user to restart/reload the harness after editing config

evals.prompt: My scanner run came back CLEAN for our checkout service. I run Karpenter and want to bring arm64 capacity into the cluster safely and cut this one service over as a canary without risking the amd64-only pods that share the cluster. Give me the NodePool and the canary Deployment pod-spec bits I need.
expectations: The NodePool uses the Karpenter v1 apiVersion `karpenter.sh/v1`.
The NodePool has a `kubernetes.io/arch` requirement pinned to `arm64`.
The output addresses how amd64-only pods are kept off the arm64 nodes (for example a NoSchedule taint on the NodePool, or an amd64 selector on those pods), with a reason.
The canary pod spec can schedule onto the arm64 NodePool: it tolerates any taint the NodePool sets.
The canary pod spec includes an arm64 `nodeSelector` (or equivalent nodeAffinity) so placement is forced, not merely permitted.
The output explains why amd64-only pods must stay off arm64 nodes: an amd64-only pod on arm64 hits CrashLoopBackOff / exec format error.
The output does not tell the user to hardcode an `-arm64` tag suffix into the Kubernetes manifest (the multi-arch manifest list handles arch selection).

knowledge_assertions.context: Must use Karpenter v1 API semantics
Must key the arch requirement/selector on kubernetes.io/arch
Must pin the kubernetes.io/arch requirement or selector to the arm64 value
Must keep amd64-only pods off the arm64 nodes: a NoSchedule taint on the arm64 NodePool or an amd64 arch selector
The canary must tolerate the arm64 taint, unless the amd64-only pods are kept off by an amd64 arch selector

evals.prompt: We push our images to ECR from GitHub Actions and it currently only builds amd64. I want every build to publish one tag that works on both amd64 and arm64 so the Graviton cutover sticks. Give me the GitHub Actions job.
expectations: The job uses the Docker buildx GitHub Action `docker/build-push-action`.
The job uses the Docker buildx GitHub Action `docker/setup-buildx-action`.
The job uses the GitHub Action `docker/setup-qemu-action` for the emulated path.
The build sets `platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64`, producing one manifest-list tag.
The build sets `push: true`.
The output explains that the `platforms` list is what turns the build into a multi-arch manifest list (one tag, right arch per node).
The output mentions the native arm64-runner alternative (per-arch builds joined via `docker buildx imagetools create`) as faster for compile-heavy workloads.
The output does not claim a single-tag manifest list requires a separate `-arm64` tag suffix.

knowledge_assertions.context: Must build both architectures into one manifest list
Must set up QEMU emulation for the single-job cross-build path
Must mention the native arm64-runner alternative
